Learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently argues that in a small portion of the acquired property, his client has put up structures decades ago and therefore, he should be permitted to retain the same by regularization or otherwise, consistent with the guarantee of constitutional right to residence u/a 19(1)(e) and right to property u/a 300A.
He also argues that, the possession of this portion of the property having not been taken away by the Respondent - BDA, the acquisition to this extent should have held to have been waived.

sentences.text:
After service of notice, learned AGA appearing for the State and learned Senior Panel Counsel appearing for the 2nd Respondent points out from the petition itself that the Petitioner was before this Court earlier in W.P.No.37838/2004 laying a challenge to the acquisition in question and the same came to be negatived vide judgment dated 1.9.2006 and further the Review Petition No.
7/2007 also has been dismissed on 07.12.2007.
Learned Panel Counsel points out that at this length of time and in the above circumstance, petition is liable to be dismissed.
The 3rd Respondent Society has filed Statement of Objections; however, its counsel is absent.
4. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the Petition Papers, this Court is broadly in agreement with the submission on behalf of the Respondents.

The Preliminary Notification u/s 17(1) issued on 19.1.1978 and this was followed by the Final Notification u/s 19(1)
issued on 28.12.1982 of the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976, the award was passed on 18.9.1986 and it was approved by the Government, as well; possession was taken on 6.10.1986 and its factum has been Gazetted vide notification dated 30.7.1987 issued under Section 16(2) of erstwhile Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
That being the position, interference of the Court is not called for.

5. The challenge to the acquisition having been negatived, in W.P No. 37838/2004 on 1.9.2006 and R.P. No. 7/2007 also having been dismissed on 07.12.2007, all the contents put forth by the petitioner for voiding the impugned endorsement have been res judicated and therefore, as rightly contended by learned Panel Counsel for the BDA, no relief can be accorded to the Petitioner.
If Petitioner desires to claim benefit under 38D of the 2020 Amendment to the BDA Act, 1976 he has to first acquiesce in the acquisition as a pre-condition.
In the above circumstances, the Petition being devoid of merits is liable to be & accordingly is rejected, costs having been reluctantly made easy.
It is made clear that this judgment shall not come in the way of compensation being claimed by the Petitioners' side, in accordance with law.
It is open to the Petitioner to claim the benefit under Section 38D of the Amended Act in accordance with law.
In that connection all contentions are kept open.

Sd/-
